transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-07-31 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (AE), Ravi Patel (SE), Anya Leduc (CSM) - Redwood; Maya Chen (Head of ML), Liam O'Donnell (CTO), Priya Kapoor (Infra Eng), Daniel Reeves (Procurement) - Orionix

Summary (auto): quick recap - customer wants renewal with capacity uplift + APAC activation; procurement wants commercial; security needs KMS and SOC2 details; SE to run quick latency tests.

[00:00] Sofia Martinez: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in today, quick agenda - renewal numbers, APAC activation plan, security blockers, and next steps.
[00:22] Maya Chen: thanks Sofia, yeah we wanted to sort out the uplift and timeline, we've got higher traffic from APAC and need a more predictable latency profile.
[00:40] Liam O'Donnell: and procurement's got a deadline of mid-August to lock the PO if possible, there's internal Q3 planning.
[01:05] Ravi Patel: quick q - when you say predictable latency, are you thinking p95 under 200ms for the payment model or are there different SLOs per endpoint?
[01:20] Maya Chen: payment definitely needs <200ms p95, fraud scoring can tolerate a bit more - up to 350ms. Our current infra has spikes in the evening in SG region where tokens take longer.
[01:48] Sofia Martinez: okay that's helpful. so two parts - capacity uplift on your committed Dedicated pool and APAC region activation. we recommended a staged activation: initial Singapore (apac-sg), then Tokyo. start with reserved Dedicated for the payment endpoints, move non-critical workloads to Hosted or burst.
[02:20] Daniel Reeves: cost question - what's the delta for Dedicated vs Hosted for that uplift? our finance wants a clear per-token and reserved capacity line item.
[02:35] Anya Leduc: we can split the proposal - show base monthly reserved commit and per-token overage; also show a hybrid model where some endpoints are hosted with fallback. we'll include numbers for quantization suggestions and batching to lower unit cost.
[03:05] Priya Kapoor: on the security side, we need to know KMS options - we use CloudKMS and an HSM-backed key for production. also need SSO/SAML and audit logs retention details.
[03:25] Ravi Patel: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; we can surface audit logs at token/route granularity. i should note the export sometimes shows slight differences in names - redwoood private was mis-typed in older docs but the capability exists.
[03:54] Maya Chen: haha okay noted. also latency benchmarking - can you run the tests with our sample prompt set? we saw weird behavior with KV cache warmup.
[04:12] Ravi Patel: yes, if you share the prompt set and a small sample set of tokens we'll run a 2-hour micro-benchmark to simulate warm/cold cache - show p50/p95/p99 and tail latency.
[04:36] Liam O'Donnell: timeline wise, if procurement signs mid-August, when can APAC go live?
[04:50] Sofia Martinez: rough timeline - contract and PO in mid-August, network prep and KMS config during week 1, pilot activation in Singapore in week 3, Tokyo follow in 6-8 weeks after pilot sign-off. so realistic go-live for critical payment endpoints late Sept to early Oct.
[05:20] Priya Kapoor: that fits our internal roadmap. i will need the firewall egress list and a contact at redwood to set up peering.
[05:33] Anya Leduc: we'll assign a network engineer; Ravi can include the minimal egress ranges.
[05:47] Daniel Reeves: procurement - we may ask for a 12-month amendment with a staged billing profile, can you reflect that in the amendment?
[06:01] Sofia Martinez: yes, we can draft an amendment that locks pricing for 12 months with defined uplift milestones. we'll include a clause for burst capacity and fallback to Hosted during spikes.
[06:23] Maya Chen: one more : about model variants - we'd like to test a quantized variant for cost reasons; does that impact latency? sometimes quantized models are faster but with some quality delta.
[06:40] Ravi Patel: tradeoff - quantization reduces memory and often speeds up throughput, but for low-latency single-request patterns it can behave differently. we'll run the quantized vs full-precision test as part of the benchmark and include quality metrics (exact match / rouge-ish) on your test prompts.
[07:10] Liam O'Donnell: any red flags re: compliance? we require SOC2 and ISO27001 and 3-year audit logs retention for certain endpoints.
[07:24] Anya Leduc: Redwood has SOC2 Type II and can provide ISO artifacts—i'll attach the latest reports. logs retention can be configured and exported to your SIEM; we'll document the retention options.
[07:46] Priya Kapoor: KMS: we need to ensure keys never leave our HSM. is there a customer-managed flow?
[07:57] Ravi Patel: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated (with Private control plane for on-prem). for Hosted we offer envelope encryption but keys can be customer-managed via KMS with limited operator access. we'll share an architecture note.
[08:25] Maya Chen: ok great. regarding fallbacks - if Dedicated capacity is saturated can we route to a cheaper hosted model? we don't want to drop requests.
[08:40] Sofia Martinez: yes policy-based routing supports failover to specified compatible models/regions. we can configure per-route fallback and throttles to preserve SLOs.
[09:02] Daniel Reeves: procurement will want a punchout or invoicing cadence - monthly invoicing preferred but we'll confirm.
[09:12] Anya Leduc: we'll make sure finance sees both monthly and annual commit pricing.
[09:35] [ambient noise interruption]
[09:50] Maya Chen: small nit - can we get a demo of the console's token-level cost breakdown? last time the UI labels were slightly off.
[10:02] Sofia Martinez: sure Anya can run a quick console walkthrough in the pilot kickoff.

[10:25] Ravi Patel: now, on the technical side - for the micro-benchmarks i'll test at sequence lengths matching your payment model (avg 64 tokens) and fraud model (avg 256 tokens), and I'll simulate burst traffic patterns 10x baseline for 15 minutes to see autoscale behavior.
[10:50] Liam O'Donnell: good. question about data residency - for some PII we need residency in SG for the pilot. can we pin region?
[11:05] Anya Leduc: yes we can pin routes and models to region; for Private deployments you get full control, for Hosted we can provision regional clusters and offer residency commitments in the contract.
[11:28] Priya Kapoor: network-wise we'll need an IP range and a contact for peering; i'll share existing network diagram.
[11:40] Sofia Martinez: perfect. i'll include network engineer contact in the follow-up.

[12:05] Maya Chen: any competitors in your experience doing better on latency? we've seen claims from CloudAIDev.
[12:18] Ravi Patel: CloudAIDev advertises microsecond claims but often with tradeoffs in batchability and model fidelity; VertexLab is strong on managed models but less mature on private KMS and auditing. we'll share a short comparison note.
[12:45] Liam O'Donnell: also we have an internal infra effort to build an in-house runtime, but timeline and ops cost pushed us toward continuing with Redwood.

[13:10] Sofia Martinez: okay quick recap and explicit next steps: we'll send updated proposal with 12-month amendment and APAC pricing, Ravi will run benchmarks and share results, Priya will provide network/KMS contacts, Daniel to confirm procurement cadence. pilot kickoff scheduled week of Aug 10.
[13:40] Daniel Reeves: yes procurement aiming to finish internal sign-off by Aug 12-14.
[13:55] Maya Chen: if benchmarks look good we want to start pilot ASAP.

[14:10] Anya Leduc: i'll attach SOC2 and recent security pack in the follow-up email and include an operations playbook for the pilot.
[14:28] Sofia Martinez: any final questions?
[14:35] Liam O'Donnell: none from me.
[14:40] Priya Kapoor: no, thanks.
[14:45] Sofia Martinez: great thanks all, we'll follow up with materials and the PO-ready amendment.

End transcript (approx 42 minutes).
questions: Can Redwood support customer-managed HSM-backed KMS?
